subject: Throughput degradation impacting Wakefield ML pipelines — remediation & commercial proposal
messages:
From: Erin Wakefield <erin.wakefield@wakefieldai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@wakefieldai.com>, Legal Ops <legal@wakefieldai.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throughput spike causing nightly pipeline failures — urgent

Jordan —

We woke up to multiple failed nightly batch runs this morning. Over the last 36 hours your API has been exhibiting elevated tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors which caused our ETL and model retrain jobs to miss SLAs for three downstream customers. This is impacting revenue recognition and we need executive attention and a proposed commercial remedy.

TL;DR:
- 99th percentile latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s for generation requests between 2027-03-30 22:00 UTC and 2027-04-01 06:00 UTC
- Error rate peaked at ~3.6% for our high-throughput endpoints
- Two scheduled model retrain windows failed and we replayed them at cost to us

Please share the incident timeline, a remediation plan, and what credit or refund you will offer per the SLA (section 5.2 in our Master Agreement). We have Legal and Ops on copy and expect a written proposal within 72 hours.

Attached is a short snapshot from our logs (wakefield_error_snapshot.png).

—Erin
VP Product, Wakefield AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Erin Wakefield <erin.wakefield@wakefieldai.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@wakefieldai.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production throughput spike causing nightly pipeline failures — urgent

Erin — thanks for the heads up and the log snapshot. I’m very sorry for the disruption; we take incidents like this seriously.

Immediate plan:
1) I’ve stood up an incident war room with our SRE and serving runtime leads and we’re doing a full timeline analysis. I’ll share a preliminary timeline by EOD Pacific.
2) Can we schedule a 30-min sync today to walk through the impact and proposed mitigation? I have availability at 13:00 or 15:30 PT.
3) I’m looping in our CSM and Sales leadership to coordinate credits/contract remediation conversations.

Cc’ing Sean Gallagher (Customer Success) and Marissa Cole (VP Sales) so we can move commercial and technical concurrently.

Attachment: redwood_incident_timeline.csv (preliminary).

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Wakefield <erin.wakefield@wakefieldai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@wakefieldai.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed commercial remedy and operational safeguards for Wakefield AI

Hi Erin / Tom — following our sync and Jordan’s timeline, we wanted to propose a concrete remediation package while we complete the root cause analysis: 

Proposed commercial remedy (good-faith, retroactive):
- A service credit equal to 25% of April 2027 invoice for the impacted endpoints (applied as a one-time credit on next invoice).
- No-penalty early access to burst capacity on Dedicated pools for 60 days so Wakefield can run retrains without queueing.
- A joint post-incident review within 10 business days and a defined SLA amendment to limit similar exposure going forward.

Operational mitigations we will enact immediately:
- Canary routing for your critical endpoints to a prioritized serving lane to reduce tail latency
- Temporary sequence-length limits and autoscaling policy tweaks during retrain windows
- Daily health exports to your Ops Slack channel until we stabilize

We want to make this right and keep Wakefield online while we complete RCA. If that sounds reasonable, Jordan and I will draft an amendment and coordinate with Legal for signatures. For reference, I’m attaching a short draft of terms (proposed_credit_terms.docx).

—Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@wakefieldai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Erin Wakefield <erin.wakefield@wakefieldai.com>, Legal Ops <legal@wakefieldai.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed commercial remedy and operational safeguards for Wakefield AI

Marissa — thanks for the quick proposal. Couple of notes from our side after internal review: 
1) The 25% credit is a good start but is low relative to our documented revenue impact; can Redwood consider a tiered credit (25% + an additional ad-hoc credit covering measurable reprocessing costs) or a fixed USD amount?
2) We need the Dedicated burst access to be guaranteed in writing (start date, capacity level).
3) Legal wants the SLA amendment language to reference the incident window and have a cap on recurrence credits.

We’re open to the post-incident review and the canary routing immediately helps. Please provide a revised term sheet and an estimate of the ad-hoc reprocessing compensation you can consider.

—Tom
Head of Ops, Wakefield AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@wakefieldai.com>, Erin Wakefield <erin.wakefield@wakefieldai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed commercial remedy and operational safeguards for Wakefield AI

Tom / Erin — appreciate the candor. Quick update on positions from Redwood: 

Commercial:
- We can increase the one-time credit to 35% of the impacted April invoice or provide a blended option: 20% invoice credit + up to $45,000 USD in documented reprocessing costs (requires receipts / scope).
- We will produce a signed addendum that guarantees Dedicated burst capacity at the following levels: 6x baseline throughput for a 60-day window starting within 5 business days of execution. Exact capacity will be documented in the addendum.

SLA amendment / legal:
- We’ll draft language that references the incident window, defines the credit calculation, and includes a recurrence cap (three similar incidents in a rolling 12-month period triggers escalation path but not automatic additional credits beyond agreed caps).

Ops / technical:
- Canary routing is live as of 2027-04-05 15:30 PT. We will provide daily latency and error exports to your Ops Slack and a final RCA within 10 business days.

Next steps: Jordan will push the term sheet to Legal and I’ll loop in our Contracts team. If Wakefield agrees to the blended credit option, we can start the addendum and schedule the post-incident review.

Thanks — Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
